sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Adams County, Washington?
sections.html:
Two county offices split the job. The Assessor decides what each parcel is worth, and the Treasurer builds the bills on those values and takes payment. Phone the Assessor at 509-659-3200 for exemptions and valuation, and use the Treasurer's office for balances and payments.

The Treasurer's duties go beyond the yearly bill. The office is also the Department of Revenue's agent for the real estate excise tax whenever property changes hands, and it conducts foreclosure on parcels that run three years behind. Under RCW 84.56.020, owners should have their statements by March 15 if the levy certifications come in on time.

sections.h2: Adams County for a property owner
sections.html:
This is wheat and irrigated farm country in eastern Washington: about 1,925 square miles of land, with only 11 or so people per square mile. Ritzville, the county seat, is in the northeast corner where Interstate 90 meets U.S. 395. Othello, in the southwest, is the biggest city. The towns are Hatton, Lind and Washtucna.

An estimated 21,488 people and 7,220 housing units were counted for 2025. From 2020 to 2024 an owner-occupied home had a median value of $273,300, and 69.3 percent of homes were lived in by their owners. A great deal of the land is working farm ground, and that affects a sale because agricultural parcels get their own excise tax treatment, described below.

Pay everything by April 30, or, if the bill tops $50, pay half by April 30 and the other half by October 31. Interest follows the schedule in RCW 84.56.020 and is charged on the whole year's tax rather than on only the late half.

EventDate or rule
Statements due outMarch 15
First half or full yearApril 30
Second halfOctober 31
Interest, house or other residence of four units or fewer9 percent a year, no penalties
Interest, other property12 percent a year, plus 3 percent on June 1 and 8 percent on December 1
Tax lien attachesJanuary 1 of the year taxes are levied (RCW 84.60.020)
Foreclosure beginsAfter three full years of delinquency (RCW 84.64.050)

A letter with an unreadable postmark still counts as timely if it reaches the Treasurer within three business days after the deadline. Interest accumulates month by month, so request a fresh payoff figure before you pay.

sections.h2: Taxes and excise tax at a sale
sections.html:
The lien for a given year's property tax starts on January 1. A sale contract may divide the year however the parties like. Without such a term, RCW 84.60.020 has the seller pay for the days before the sale and the buyer for the days after. Escrow instructions usually handle the split, so read yours.

Each transfer also requires a Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit. File it with the Treasurer first; only then can the deed be recorded at the Auditor. An incomplete affidavit is turned away, and forms go on legal-size paper (8.5 by 14 inches).

  • Excise tax is due 30 days after the sale date. For this purpose the Department of Revenue counts the notarized deed date as the sale date.
  • On top of the state portion, the county adds a local 0.25 percent of the price and a $5 processing fee.
  • State rates climb in steps: 1.1 percent on the first slice, then 1.28, 2.75 and 3.0 percent.
  • Agricultural or timberland pays a flat 1.28 percent state rate when the buyer keeps using it that way and the Assessor signs the Notice of Continuance on the affidavit.

With so much land in farms, that final rule comes up often. If you are selling wheat ground or an irrigated parcel, phone the Assessor ahead of closing rather than afterward.

sections.h2: How do you challenge an assessed value?
sections.html:
The route is a petition to the county board of equalization, filed on a Department of Revenue form. RCW 84.40.038 sets the deadline as the latest of three dates: July 1 of the assessment year, 30 days after the notice was mailed or sent electronically, or a county-adopted limit that can reach 60 days.

A late petition can still be heard if it arrives within a reasonable time and the owner shows good cause. Recognized causes include a death or serious illness in the immediate family, wrong written advice from assessor or board staff, a natural disaster, and a postal delay that the Postal Service documents. To learn which deadline your notice carries, call the Assessor at 509-659-3200.

Adams County has an exemption for seniors and people with disabilities, handled by the Assessor. To qualify you must be at least 61 on December 31 of the application year, live in the home as your principal residence on up to one acre, and have household income of $41,000 or less.

  • RCW 84.36.381 also covers people retired because of disability and people receiving VA compensation at a service-connected rating of 40 percent or higher.
  • A seller or displaced owner can move the exemption to a replacement home, though only one home per year can claim it.
  • Statements include a note about the state deferral program in chapter 84.38 RCW.
  • The Washington Homeownership Resource Center, at 877-894-4663, helps with mortgage or tax trouble.

sections.h2: What happens when taxes go unpaid for three years?
sections.html:
Foreclosure begins with the Treasurer. Each July a Certificate of Delinquency goes to Adams County Superior Court, foreclosure costs start to add up, and a title search is done on every parcel. Certified mail goes to everyone with a recorded interest, and the county's official newspaper carries a published notice.

  • A judgment then forecloses the tax lien and authorizes a public auction.
  • Owners and other interested parties may still redeem until closing time the day before the sale.
  • Unsold parcels become Tax Title Property, held by the county in trust. Email the Treasurer for the list.
  • No certificate is filed when the delinquent tax is $100 or less, not counting interest and penalties (RCW 84.64.050).

Personal property is handled separately and is not part of a house sale.

sections.h2: Preparing a cash sale of an Adams County property
sections.html: With no lender, a sale moves on a timetable you and the buyer agree on. Before you list or answer an offer, do four things. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff. Ask the Assessor whether the parcel carries an agricultural classification or a senior exemption. Ask your escrow officer how the year's tax will be divided. And plan the excise tax paperwork: the affidavit reaches the Treasurer before the deed reaches the Auditor, and payment is due within 30 days of the sale date.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Adams County, WA?
faqs.a: The whole bill is due April 30, or half on April 30 and half on October 31 if it is over $50. Late amounts accrue interest by the month.

faqs.q: What is the interest rate on late taxes in Adams County?
faqs.a: Homes with up to four units pay the lower rate and no penalties, while other property pays a higher yearly rate plus two later penalties. The table above has the figures.

faqs.q: Who pays real estate excise tax when I sell in Adams County?
faqs.a: Normally the seller, though the buyer becomes responsible if the seller fails to pay. The Treasurer takes it with the affidavit, ahead of recording.

faqs.q: How long does Adams County wait before foreclosing for unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Three full years. A Certificate of Delinquency then goes to Superior Court in July, and you can still redeem before the auction.

faqs.q: Who can I call about the senior exemption in Adams County?
faqs.a: The Assessor's Office, 509-659-3200. Age, residence, acreage and income limits apply, and the section above spells them out.
